newsitem.title: UK: Cuba, Iran feature heavily on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Cuba, Iran feature heavily on sugar freight market.

text.p: Cuba and Iran dominated Tuesday's list of quoted origins and destinations on the sugar freight market in a wealth of fixed and new business, shipbrokers said.

Shipments of Cuban sugar are said to be tight into January as the first supplies trickle out from the 1996/97 cane crop, while Iranian demand for both white and raw sugar continues apace over the pre-Ramadan period.
Pacol was said to have fixed its recent order for 30,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Iran for early January but was still open for 25,000 tonnes to the Black Sea for mid-January.
Alpine fixed its mid-January Cuban inquiry for 20/22,000 tonnes to the Black Sea in the high $20 bracket.

Shipbrokers said Eurasia Expresslines was open for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Eemshaven to Iran for end-December while Iranian shippers Bosco quoted for 14,000 tonnes, again bagged, from Continent to Iran for any December dates.

Other firmer business came from E D & F Man, said to have fixed 12,000 tonnes in bulk from Maceio to Manfredonia for end-January. Man also quoted for 17,500 tonnes from the same origin to Durban for mid-January.
Louis Dreyfus fixed 12/13,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to Colombo for early January and Brazilian shippers SIMAB fixed a prompt 14,000-tonne bagged cargo from north Brazil to Lagos.

Czarnikow fixed 12,000 tonnes in bags from Thailand to east Africa with options of Colombo, Pakistan and Bangladesh for December dates and Genoc quoted for a prompt 3/5,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Poland to Mediterranean or Aqaba.

Elsewhere, market sources said the results of Iraq's tender to buy sugar under the U.N. oil-for-food deal would be slow to emerge as the financing arrangements would demand scrutiny from various parties and the tender restrictions were numerous.
